senses.gloss: f. a species of oak from which the gall-nut is collected (quercus infectoria), or the acorns of which are used as tanning material (quercus aegilops or Oak of Bashan) [not ash-tree].
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Middot 3:7">Midd. III, 7</cite> <he>מלתראות של מ׳</he> (some ed. <cite ref="M01168"><he>מילה</he></cite>, Maim. <he>מילת</he>) beams of Milla; <cite ref="Eruvin 3a:1">Erub. 3ᵃ</cite> Ms. M. (ed. <cite ref="M01168"><he>מילה</he></cite>); <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 17:1">Lev. R. s. 17</cite>, beg.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 5:3">Tosef. Shebi. V, 3</cite> <he>עלי מילת</he> leaves of the Millath (prob. used for steeping in wine or oil).

Ib. (missing in ed. Zuck.) עיקר מלת the real Millath-nut(?).]—Pl. מִילִּין. Ib. VII, 11; Y. ib. IX, 38ᵈ bot.; Pes. 53ᵃ סימן להרים מ׳ an indication of highlands is the growth of Milla-trees.—מֵי מ׳ a solution of acorns; also a solution of gall-nuts.

<cite ref="Gittin 19a:15">Gitt. 19ᵃ</cite> (v. <cite ref="A02773"><he>אֲפַץ</he></cite>) <he>שאין מי מ׳ על גבי מי מ׳</he> (Ar. <he>ע״ג מ׳</he>) for a tanned ink will not take on a tanned hide. Y. ib. II, 44ᵇ top: when one desires to write a secret letter to his friend, <he>הוא כתב במי מ׳ והך דמקבל וכ׳</he> he writes with a solution of gall-nut, and the recipient of the letter pours over it untanned ink which settles on the writing.
